speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development what are the current waiting times for children and adults with disabilities to get their assessments made by psychologists, speech therapists and other trained personnel.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Compared to 2014, both figures have shown an improvement.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Some of the children need to be assessed for suitability for early intervention programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, the Development Support Programme (DSP) supports children with milder needs who are in mainstream preschools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC) serves preschoolers with more severe needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Students in our mainstream schools can be referred for assessment conducted by MOE psychologists.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Such referrals are prioritised jointly between the school and the MOE psychologist based on the urgency and severity of the child's needs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Adults with disabilities may also require assessments for suitability for a range of Government-funded programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: After assessment, some of the children and adults may have to find a place to receive the appropriate service.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF is working with VWOs and other Government agencies to further improve both the waiting times for assessment, as well as the time for subsequent placements into the most suitable services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will continue to expand the capacity and improve the delivery of services for both children and adults with disabilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are also working on manpower initiatives, such as developing hubs that employ psychologists and therapists so that their services, which are needed for assessments and intervention, can be rendered more efficiently.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But if the response is that the waiting times have improved, then I am heartened to hear so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I hope that we can continue to monitor this because, as you can imagine, the parents are anxious when it is an initial diagnosis that needs to be made, especially in the case of EIPIC for infants and children where I think they are really starting very early these days.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The earlier the intervention starts, the better the success and outcomes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And particularly, for EIPIC, we are also increasing, the number of places available.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Following that, we have also planned for three other centres within the next three years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: All in all, by 2018, we should be able to have 3,200 EIPIC places in Singapore.
